instruction: I want to ensure all my connections are secure by using HTTPS-Only mode. Can you enable this security feature in Chrome?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"https_first_mode_enabled":false}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable HTTPS-Only mode (also known as HTTPS-First mode) in Chrome. The evaluator checks https_first_mode_enabled field in Chrome Preferences. Initial state: false. Expected state: true.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts the https_first_mode_enabled preference from Chrome Preferences file
Metric logic correctly performs exact string comparison between result and expected value
Expected value is semantically correct ("true" for enabled HTTPS-Only mode)
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to ensure preferences are written to disk and can be read
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the exact setting required by the instruction (HTTPS-Only mode = https_first_mode_enabled)
Proper exception handling in getter for missing files, invalid JSON, and unsupported OS types
Data flow is correct: getter returns "true"/"false" → metric compares with expected "true" → returns 1.0 on match
